# Permits and inspections

What the city building department told us at the counter.

## Work that needs a permit

New structure and additions; removing or moving a load-bearing wall; new decks over 30 inches high; a new roof structure; changes to the electrical service or panel; any new gas line; new plumbing or moving drains; and replacing a furnace or water heater. A permit also covers a new fence over 6 feet.

## Work that usually does not

Painting, flooring, cabinets, countertops, replacing a fixture or an outlet with the same kind, and ordinary repairs. When unsure, call the department: it is a free call.

## Inspection stages

A permit comes with inspections at set stages: footings before concrete, framing before the walls are closed up, rough-in of wiring and pipes, insulation, and a final inspection. The inspector signs the card when each stage passes, and work must not be covered until then.

## Unpermitted work and selling the house

Work done without a permit has to be disclosed when you sell and can hold up the sale. A buyer's inspector may ask that finished walls be opened to check the work.

## Who pulls the permit

A licensed contractor normally pulls the permit for their own work. A homeowner can often pull it for work on their own home, and then takes responsibility for the inspections.
